findings.issue_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses [z.string().toString()] as computed property keys, producing meaningless fixed string keys like "ZodString" instead of intended dynamic validation patterns, making the schema fundamentally broken and unable to validate token responses correctly

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod SafeParseResult object but CalendarService.ts assigns it directly to key and stores it via prisma.credential.update, corrupting the stored credential by saving { success: true, data: {...} } instead of the actual credential object
`z.string().toString()` evaluates to `"[object Object]"` at runtime, breaking the intended dynamic key matching in `minimumTokenResponseSchema` and causing expiry-field validation to never be applied

Zod strips unknown keys by default, so when the minimum schema is used, `refresh_token` and `expiry_date` are removed from `data`; the code then sets `data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` (a literal string), destroying the actual refresh token and making future refreshes fail

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseReturnType` (`{ success, data }`), but Google's CalendarService assigns this wrapper directly to `key` in the `prisma.credential.update` call without accessing `.data`, corrupting the stored credential

`refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `Response` object when sync is enabled but returns integration-specific parsed objects otherwise; no caller handles the `Response` type, causing runtime crashes (e.g., Google's `res?.data` would be `undefined`)
The webhook handler in `app-credential.ts` never checks `req.method`, allowing GET, PUT, DELETE, etc. to create or update credentials
`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws on invalid input with no try/catch, producing a 500 error instead of a 400 with a meaningful message
`symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` on the keys in `app-credential.ts` have no error handling; malformed, tampered, or wrongly-keyed input causes an unhandled exception and a 500 response
The webhook secret in `app-credential.ts` is compared with `!==`, which is vulnerable to timing attacks; a constant-time comparison should be used
The `fetch()` call to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` has no timeout, no status-code check, and no try/catch; network errors or non-200 responses propagate unhandled
The POST to the credential sync endpoint in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` includes no auth headers, webhook secret, or API key, leaving the endpoint unauthenticated

Salesforce's token-refresh code calls Salesforce's API directly and does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so when credential sharing is enabled it bypasses the sync endpoint entirely, making the feature inconsistent
The redirect URI in `zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` was changed from `appConfig.slug` to the hardcoded literal string `"zoho-bigin"`, losing dynamic configuration
No unit or integration tests were added for the new webhook endpoint (`app-credential.ts`), token-refresh abstraction (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), or response parser (`parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`)
CalendarService.ts Salesforce token refresh is unconditional, running on every service construction rather than only when the token is expired
CalendarService.ts Salesforce token refresh doesn't use the new refreshOAuthTokens wrapper like every other app in the PR
CalendarService.ts Salesforce token refresh doesn't route through CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT even when credential sharing is enabled

refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns inconsistent types — raw fetch Response when credential sharing is enabled vs app-specific return types when disabled, causing runtime failures in Google, Hubspot, and Zoho consumers
refreshOAuthTokens.ts never .json()-parses the Response object, so apps like Zoom/Office365/Webex/Lark that might tolerate a Response won't get usable JSON

parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:6-11 Zod schema uses [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] which both evaluate to '[object Object]', causing key collision and effectively validating nothing
parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23 fabricates refresh_token with literal string 'refresh_token' when missing, which gets persisted to credentials instead of raising an error
.env.example CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY comment says key must be 32 bytes for AES256 but suggested command 'openssl rand -base64 24' produces only 24 bytes (192 bits)
zoho-bigin CalendarService.ts passes credentialId instead of credential.userId to refreshOAuthTokens, inconsistent with all other call sites
zoho-bigin api/add.ts changes redirect URI to hardcoded '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback' instead of using appConfig.slug, an unrelated behavior change
createOAuthAppCredential.ts:6 imports decodeOAuthState as '../oauth/decodeOAuthState' instead of './decodeOAuthState' after the file was moved to _utils/oauth/
app-credential.ts webhook handler does not restrict HTTP method, accepting any verb with a body
app-credential.ts webhook handler does not wrap Zod parse in try/catch, producing unhandled 500 instead of clean 400 on validation failure
app-credential.ts uses process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || '' allowing decryption to silently proceed with an empty key if env var is missing

refreshOAuthTokens.ts independently requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT at call site, inconsistent with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED feature flag gating in constants.ts, causing silent fallback to direct provider refresh when misconfigured

`minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed property keys that evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a dynamic/wildcard key, causing all token fields except `access_token` to be silently discarded when credential sharing is enabled
When `refresh_token` is absent from parsed data, it is set to the literal string "refresh_token" instead of a real value, guaranteeing all subsequent token refresh attempts will fail

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `SafeParseResult` wrapper but is assigned directly to `key` and stored as the credential, so the persisted credential becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` instead of the token data

When the sync endpoint is used, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` but callers expect the return type of their original refresh function, causing runtime TypeErrors or undefined access

TOCTOU race condition: `findFirst` + conditional `create` allows two concurrent webhook deliveries to both create duplicate credentials; should use `upsert` with a composite unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`

`appConfig.slug` was replaced with the hardcoded string "zoho-bigin" in the redirect URI, coupling the URL to a literal and defeating the purpose of the config-driven slug

refresh_token is set to the literal string "refresh_token" as a fallback instead of preserving the existing credential's refresh token, causing all subsequent token refreshes to fail

refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response when credential sharing is enabled, but multiple callers (Google Calendar, Hubspot, Zoho Bigin, Zoho CRM) expect a different type with .data/.access_token/.expires_in properties, causing runtime errors

Salesforce CalendarService does not wrap its token refresh in refreshOAuthTokens like all other integrations, so Salesforce credentials never participate in credential sync even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is set
Dead code in Salesforce CalendarService: the success check after parseRefreshTokenResponse is unreachable because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so success is always true if it returns
Hardcoded slug "zoho-bigin" replaces dynamic appConfig.slug in the OAuth redirect URI, which will silently break if the slug in config.json ever changes
Non-constant-time comparison of webhook authentication secret using JavaScript `!==` operator, which leaks timing information and allows progressive secret recovery by an attacker

Decrypted credential keys are stored with zero schema validation after JSON.parse, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary JSON as credentials for any userId/appSlug pair including payment apps like Stripe

Broken Zod catch-all schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` that evaluate to a fixed string instead of catch-all patterns, causing all fields except access_token to pass through unchecked

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The webhook handler in `app-credential.ts` never checks `req.method`, allowing GET, PUT, DELETE, etc. to create or update credentials

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the exported `handler` never checks `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). After validating a shared secret header, it immediately `parse`s `req.body` and proceeds to `prisma.credential.update` / `prisma.credential.create`. In Next.js API routes, this means any HTTP method (GET/PUT/DELETE/etc.) that includes the correct header and a valid body can trigger the same credential create/update logic. So the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and `JSON.parse(...)` on the keys in `app-credential.ts` have no error handling; malformed, tampered, or wrongly-keyed input causes an unhandled exception and a 500 response
The webhook secret in `app-credential.ts` is compared with `!==`, which is vulnerable to timing attacks; a constant-time comparison should be used

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook authentication check compares a header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using JavaScript string inequality (`!==`). Standard string comparisons are not constant-time and can short-circuit on the first differing character, creating a potential timing side-channel when comparing secrets. A constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on normalized buffers) would avoid this class of issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `fetch()` call to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` has no timeout, no status-code check, and no try/catch; network errors or non-200 responses propagate unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when syncing is enabled it does `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `Response` without any `response.ok`/status handling, without a timeout/abort signal, and without local try/catch. A network failure will reject the promise and (unless every caller wraps it) bubble up; a non-2xx response will be treated as a successful return value at this layer. These behaviors are directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The POST to the credential sync endpoint in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` includes no auth headers, webhook secret, or API key, leaving the endpoint unauthenticated

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` indeed sends only a POST body (`URLSearchParams` with `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`) and sets no explicit auth headers/secret. However, the finding’s conclusion that this “leaves the endpoint unauthenticated” is not verifiable from the diff: the endpoint is external to this repo and could be authenticated/secured via other mechanisms (network-level controls, mTLS, IP allowlisting, or endpoint-specific logic), and the code even comments that the payload should be customized to the endpoint’s requirements. So the diff shows no auth headers, but not a definite defect that the endpoint is unauthenticated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refreshOAuthTokens.ts returns inconsistent types — raw fetch Response when credential sharing is enabled vs app-specific return types when disabled, causing runtime failures in Google, Hubspot, and Zoho consumers

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, but returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns otherwise (`any`). In the diff, some callers assume a non-`Response` shape:
- **GoogleCalendarService**: `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so when sharing is enabled `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token`/`token.expiry_date` will throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed property keys that evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]", not a dynamic/wildcard key, causing all token fields except `access_token` to be silently discarded when credential sharing is enabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS object literal, these computed keys are evaluated immediately and become fixed string property names (very likely something like "[object Object]"), not a wildcard/index signature. Zod does not treat these as “any string key” rules; instead it will expect those literal properties to exist, and by default it strips unknown keys. So when credential sharing is enabled, typical token responses (e.g., `{access_token, expires_in, refresh_token, ...}`) won’t match this schema as intended (they may fail validation, and extra fields will not be preserved).

adjudication_records.issue_text: When the sync endpoint is used, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` but callers expect the return type of their original refresh function, causing runtime TypeErrors or undefined access

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy (it calls `fetch(...)` and returns that Response). - `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: it assumes `res` has an axios-like `.data` (`const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`). A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race condition: `findFirst` + conditional `create` allows two concurrent webhook deliveries to both create duplicate credentials; should use `upsert` with a composite unique constraint on `(userId, appId)`

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) does a non-atomic check-then-act sequence: it `findFirst` for an existing credential by `{ userId, appId }` and then either `update` or `create`. If two webhook requests for the same `(userId, appId)` arrive concurrently, both can observe “no credential” and both attempt `create`, which can result in duplicate rows if the DB schema doesn’t enforce uniqueness, or a thrown unique-constraint error/500 if it does. This is a classic TOCTOU race inherent in the diff; an atomic `upsert` (using a composite unique key) or equivalent transaction/locking would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts uses z.string().toString() as computed property key, which yields "[object Object]" instead of accepting arbitrary keys, defeating the purpose of the minimum token response schema

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Webhook secret comparison uses !== instead of a constant-time comparison function, making it vulnerable to timing attacks on an endpoint that can create or update credentials for any user

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler at `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` authenticates requests solely by comparing a header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==`. In Node/JS, normal string equality comparison is not constant-time and can short-circuit, which is why security-sensitive secret comparisons are typically done with a constant-time primitive (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`). Since this endpoint can create/update credentials for an arbitrary `userId` in the request body and the shared secret is the main protection, using a non-constant-time comparison is a verifiable security weakness present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing try-catch around symmetricDecrypt and JSON.parse in the webhook endpoint, causing unstructured 500 errors instead of consistent JSON error responses when decryption or parsing fails

If `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing/incorrect, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` can throw, and if decryption yields non-JSON, `JSON.parse(...)` will throw. Those exceptions will bubble out of the handler and result in a generic/unstructured 500 response rather than a consistent `res.status(...).json(...)` error payload, unlike the explicit 403/404 responses used elsewhere in the handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-constant-time comparison of webhook authentication secret using JavaScript `!==` operator, which leaks timing information and allows progressive secret recovery by an attacker

adjudication.rationale:
In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the secret is validated via a direct inequality check:


JavaScript string/byte comparisons using `===`/`!==` are not constant-time and may short-circuit based on the first differing byte/character, which can leak timing information about how much of the secret matches. adjudication_records.issue_text: Decrypted credential keys are stored with zero schema validation after JSON.parse, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary JSON as credentials for any userId/appSlug pair including payment apps like Stripe

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted `keys` payload is handled as `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys }})` / `create({ data: { key: keys, ... }})` with no schema validation of the parsed JSON against the expected credential shape for the given `appSlug`/`appMetadata.type`. The only gate is a shared-secret header check, and the request body allows arbitrary `userId` and `appSlug`, so anyone who can call this webhook with the secret can set arbitrary JSON as credentials for any existing user and any app present in `appStoreMetadata`/DB. adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken Zod catch-all schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys `[z.string().toString()]` that evaluate to a fixed string instead of catch-all patterns, causing all fields except access_token to pass through unchecked

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. In a JS object literal, computed keys must evaluate to concrete string/symbol values at runtime; `z.string().toString()` does not create a Zod “catch-all” for arbitrary keys, it produces a fixed property name (and the two computed keys are just two fixed names). Therefore this schema does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” behavior; arbitrary fields like `expires_in`/`expiry_date` will not be validated as numbers (and, with default Zod object behavior, are likely stripped rather than validated). This is a real, verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing refresh_token in token response defaults to the literal string "refresh_token" instead of proper handling, enabling credential substitution when combined with the broken schema validation
